landing.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
landing.faq.subtitle: A few common questions about the platform
landing.faq.q1.q: What is Yuvi Spark and what is it for?
landing.faq.q1.a: Yuvi Spark is an AI-powered personalized learning platform built for the Ministry of Education's 720 program. It maps each student's learning path and adapts content, pace, and difficulty accordingly, alongside a smart learning companion and a clear picture for the teaching staff.
landing.faq.q2.q: How does learning actually work in Yuvi Spark?
landing.faq.q2.a: The journey starts with a short learner mapping process that identifies strengths, interests, and learning preferences. As learning continues, the system adjusts content and pace based on progress, and gives the student encouraging, non-numeric feedback. At the same time, the teacher receives clear insights into the class's progress.
landing.faq.q3.q: How does the AI work in the system?
landing.faq.q3.a: The smart learning agent accompanies the student along the way, responds in the selected language (Hebrew, Arabic, or English), and helps explain material - without replacing the teacher. The AI never receives identifying student details, and every insight shown to a teacher comes with an explanation and the underlying data, to keep things fully transparent.
landing.faq.q4.q: What data and privacy protections are in place?
landing.faq.q4.a: Yuvi Spark shares only general learning-profile details with the AI engine, never personally identifying information. All learning data, language preference, and progress are stored securely, and students are always told when they are using an AI tool.
landing.faq.q5.q: What happens if a student struggles or falls behind?
landing.faq.q5.a: When the system detects difficulty or a slower pace, it shows the teacher a clear insight along with the reasoning behind it - not just a score. The teacher decides how to respond: reinforcing a topic, adjusting a task, or having a personal check-in with the student.
landing.faq.q6.q: Who can use Yuvi Spark and how do schools join?
landing.faq.q6.a: The platform is intended for students, teachers, and pedagogical staff at schools participating in the 720 program. Joining and rollout are coordinated with the school's staff according to Ministry of Education guidelines, so it fits the specific needs of each class and student.

YuviStudio.tut.bench.title: The room design table
YuviStudio.tut.bench.what: Put the room design table on the lit patch, in the far left corner.
YuviStudio.tut.bench.why: The table is the station you decorate the room from. In the corner it stays out of the middle of the room.
YuviStudio.tut.bench.howPick: Press the button and the table moves onto your cursor.
YuviStudio.tut.bench.howDrop: The table is on your cursor — click inside the green circle to put it down.
YuviStudio.tut.bench.tip: Click outside the circle and the preview turns red — the table stays in your hands.
YuviStudio.tut.turn.title: Turn it the right way round
YuviStudio.tut.turn.what: Turn the table until it faces the arrow, into the room.
YuviStudio.tut.turn.why: You stand in front of the table to use it, so it has to face the room and not the wall.
YuviStudio.tut.turn.how: Each press turns it a quarter turn. Four presses land it exactly right.
YuviStudio.tut.turn.tip: You can turn any piece of furniture later: hover over it and choose Rotate.
YuviStudio.tut.turn.tip.touch: You can turn any piece of furniture later: press and hold it and choose Rotate.
YuviStudio.tut.platform.title: Yuvi's platform
YuviStudio.tut.platform.what: Now Yuvi's platform — the station you dress him from. This time there is no fixed corner.
YuviStudio.tut.platform.why: This room is yours. You decide where each station stands.
YuviStudio.tut.platform.howPick: Press the button and the platform moves onto your cursor.
YuviStudio.tut.platform.howDrop: Click anywhere on clear floor to put the platform down.
YuviStudio.tut.platform.tip: Furniture cannot stand inside other furniture, so some spots will show in red.
YuviStudio.tut.done.title: Your room is ready
YuviStudio.tut.done.what: You moved and turned both stations — that is everything room design asks of you.
YuviStudio.tut.done.why: The same moves work on every piece of furniture you add: pick up, put down, turn.
YuviStudio.tut.done.how: Stand on the room design table to open the furniture store.
YuviStudio.tut.done.tip: You can always move a station again: hover over it and choose Move.

tch.help.subjectFilter: The subject filter is in the top bar and applies to every panel on screen at once.
tch.help.attentionInbox: "Needs you now" sits at the top of Home. Every row expands to the raw datum that triggered it.
tch.help.evidence: Every number here opens up — clicking "why?" shows the underlying events.
tch.help.goals: The mentoring screen holds the class picture — who awaits approval and who you last talked to. Each student’s profile holds their own loop: documenting a talk, goals, and approving them.
tch.help.goalApproval: Approving a goal grants the student sparks. If it was already summarized or the daily cap is reached, no sparks are added — and that is shown.
tch.help.subGroups: In the learning-gaps panel you can assign one goal to every student struggling with the same topic.
tch.help.liveClassroom: The live strip at the top of Home shows who is online, in a lesson, or struggling — always with a "last seen".
tch.help.alerts: Alerts arrive in realtime and persist until resolved. Each one carries its evidence.
tch.help.notes: Notes come in three levels: private, shared with the student, and a directive Yuvi will use when talking to them.
tch.help.coachDirective: A note marked as a directive changes what Yuvi says to the student. It is off by default.
tch.help.customTasks: The task builder writes a lesson, questions and an answer key from your request. Automatic quality checks run on the result and flag, per item, what to look at — they guide, never block; the call is always the teacher's. Before sending you can edit without limit: an AI edit that takes a plain description of the change ("make question 3 easier"), or a full regenerate. The preview is exactly what the student sees, with the answer key behind a toggle. After sending the content is frozen — a task never changes under a student mid-attempt.
tch.help.notifications: The bell holds personal updates. Dismissing keeps the record — you can show it again.
tch.help.groups: Groups are managed in the admin console. A teacher is linked to a group; a student is enrolled in it.
tch.help.noComparisons: The system never compares or ranks students — a Ministry of Education requirement.
tch.help.privacy: You see only students in your groups. A student's conversations with Yuvi are not exposed — except distress flags.

tour.teacher.welcome.title: Hi, I'm Yuvi
tour.teacher.welcome.body: I sit with your students while they learn, and here I help you too. Let me show you where everything is — every number on this dashboard opens to the data it was computed from.
tour.teacher.live.title: Who's here right now
tour.teacher.live.body: Who is online, who is inside a lesson, and who is stuck. The dot updates live, and it always says when they were last seen — an absence is not an event.
tour.teacher.pulse.title: Class pulse
tour.teacher.pulse.body: Engagement, active time, and progress against learning objectives. These are group numbers — nothing here, or anywhere in the product, compares one student to another.
tour.teacher.gaps.title: Shared gaps
tour.teacher.gaps.body: Topics several students are stuck on together. From here you can set one goal for a whole sub-group in a click.
tour.teacher.scope.title: What you are looking at
tour.teacher.scope.body: Pick a class, a sub-group and a subject here — the choice follows you across every screen and survives a reload. Anything you have narrowed to is marked here, and one click clears it.
tour.teacher.bell.title: Alerts
tour.teacher.bell.body: Anything urgent arrives here. Clicking a row takes you to exactly the thing it is about.
tour.teacher.assistant.title: Ask me
tour.teacher.assistant.body: Ask me about a student or about the group. I answer only from what was actually measured, and I show you which data I pulled — if I don't have a figure, I say so.
tour.teacher.roster.title: Your students
tour.teacher.roster.body: Filter by status, subject, or who is online. Clicking a card opens the full profile.
tour.teacher.profile.title: Student profile
tour.teacher.profile.body: Everything known about one student, split into tabs: mastery, activity, goals, badges, reflections, and your own notes.
tour.teacher.goals.title: Progress against objectives
tour.teacher.goals.body: Progress by subject and learning objective. From the Goals tab you can set a new goal, approve a completed one, and award the student sparks.
tour.teacher.evidence.title: Every number opens
tour.teacher.evidence.body: This is the principle of the whole dashboard: every recommendation, flag, and gap has a button that shows the raw datum behind it. If something cannot be explained, it is not shown.
tour.learner.welcome.title: Hi {name}, great to meet you!
tour.learner.welcome.body: I'm Yuvi, and I'm with you on every screen. Let's take a quick spin so you know where everything is.
tour.learner.next.title: Pick up here
tour.learner.next.body: This is the next step I lined up. One click to start, or carry on from exactly where we stopped.
tour.learner.map.title: Your activeness map
tour.learner.map.body: Six areas that make up how you learn. The further a corner sits from the middle, the stronger that area. Hover a circle to see what moved this week, and why.
tour.learner.subjects.title: Your subjects
tour.learner.subjects.body: Every subject and its track. See what's behind us, what's on the table now, and reopen any topic.
tour.learner.goals.title: Your goals
tour.learner.goals.body: Small goals that can be reached, alone or together with your teacher. A goal that's done gets marked, and on to the next one.
tour.learner.studio.title: The studio
tour.learner.studio.body: This opens my room, where you design me: colours, gear and furniture. It's the place to make things.
tour.learner.badgesDoor.title: Now for the medals
tour.learner.badgesDoor.body: Click your picture here, then "My badges" — I'll meet you there.
tour.learner.badges.title: Badges and medals
tour.learner.badges.body: Everything you finish collects a badge. See what's been earned, what's close, and pick one to be the profile picture.
tour.learner.companion.title: And I'll stay right here
tour.learner.companion.body: In this corner I'm always around. A question about an exercise, something that didn't work out, or just a thought — click me and let's talk. That's the spin done — have fun!
tour.lesson.welcome.title: Your first lesson, {name}!
tour.lesson.welcome.body: Before you start — a quick look at how a lesson works, and what to do when something feels hard.
tour.lesson.stage.title: The lesson happens here
tour.lesson.stage.body: Everything you read, watch and answer shows up in this area. Take it at your own pace — nothing here is timed.
tour.lesson.door.title: Stuck? Press me
tour.lesson.door.body: I'm right here through the whole lesson. Give me a click and I'll open up.
tour.lesson.ask.title: Ask me anything
tour.lesson.ask.body: Write in your own words — 'I don't get this', or 'explain it differently'. There's no wrong way to ask.
tour.lesson.help.title: A nudge or a full explanation
tour.lesson.help.body: On a question you can ask for a hint that gets you moving, or an explanation that goes over the whole idea again.
tour.lesson.hand.title: Or call your teacher
tour.lesson.hand.body: If I'm not enough, this button tells your teacher you need them. Asking for help is a smart move, not a last resort.
tour.lesson.path.title: Where you are in the lesson
tour.lesson.path.body: Switch between talking to me and seeing your path — what's done, what you're on, and what's next.
tour.lesson.stay.title: Off you go
tour.lesson.stay.body: I'll be here the whole way. Answer at your pace, and call me the moment something stops making sense. Good luck!

tch.tasks.difficulty.explain.easy: One step per question. Numbers are chosen so the arithmetic is never the difficulty, and the question names the method to use. Wrong options are careless slips, everything stays inside what the lesson worked through, and the hint spells out the first step.
tch.tasks.difficulty.explain.medium: Most questions take two steps, with ordinary numbers — the fractions, decimals or negatives the topic uses. The question states a situation without naming the method, every wrong option encodes a real misconception, and about a quarter apply the idea to a situation the lesson did not show.
tch.tasks.difficulty.explain.hard: Most questions take three steps or combine two ideas, with awkward numbers and edge cases (zero, negatives, unit conversion). No scaffolding in the wording, sometimes a fact that is not needed, every wrong option a misconception, and at least a third ask for transfer or for why.
tch.tasks.difficulty.explainSlides: In a presentation the level sets the pace: easy spends its slides on the basics with a worked example on each; hard covers them quickly and spends the deck on the harder cases and on why the method works.
